title: Eye test and glasses
what: The doctor checks how clearly you see and finds the lenses that help you see better. It is painless.
why: If your distance or near vision got worse, your eyes get tired, or reading gives you headaches. Also for a checkup or to replace old glasses.
duration: usually 20 to 40 minutes, longer if your pupils are dilated
tell_doctor: If you wear contact lenses, which kind and for how long

prepare.title: Contact lenses
prepare.text: Soft lenses are usually taken out 1 to 2 days before, hard lenses earlier. Check with your clinic.

prepare.title: Getting home
prepare.text: If you get drops to widen your pupils, you cannot drive for a few hours afterwards.

steps: You sit in front of a chart with letters or symbols
You cover one eye and read the lines, then the other eye
A machine quickly measures how your eye bends light
The doctor puts different lenses in a trial frame and asks which is better
Sometimes the pressure in your eye is measured and the back of the eye is checked
You get a prescription for glasses
feel: After drops to widen the pupils, bright light is harsh and close things look blurry for a few hours
after: You get your glasses prescription right away
It usually takes a few days to get used to new glasses
If you still do not see well after 1 to 2 weeks, go back to the doctor
red_flags: Sudden loss of vision, flashes of light, a curtain over your vision, or severe eye pain: see a doctor right away or call emergency services

faq.q: Can I choose glasses without a doctor?
faq.a: Ready-made glasses do not match your eyes exactly. It is better to have a specialist check your eyes and write a prescription.

faq.q: Do glasses make my eyes worse?
faq.a: No. The right glasses do not make your vision worse. Without them, you just notice how you really see.

faq.q: How often should I have my eyes checked?
faq.a: Adults usually every 1 to 2 years. After 40 and with diabetes, more often, as your doctor advises.
